items.title: AI auditors catch most agent misbehavior but flood reviewers with false alarms, new study finds
items.summary: AI models can often spot problematic behavior by other AI agents in logs, according to a study by Anthropic researcher Andy Hall. GPT-5 found about 98 percent of reward-hacking cases, but the more exhaustively the search is tuned, the more false alarms pile up. That's not yet enough for reliable safety checks....

items.title: OpenAI released a new cybersecurity model. Is that enough?
items.summary: OpenAI's newest cybersecurity model comes out as AI labs face scrutiny of their work to protect digital infrastructure.

items.title: GPT‑6 Cyber: Advancing the frontier of aligned cybersecurity agents
items.summary: Introducing GPT‑6 Cyber, OpenAI’s cybersecurity model for finding exploitable vulnerabilities and developing fixes, trained to stay within authorized scope.

items.title: The gap between open and closed AI models in cyber capabilities keeps shrinking
items.summary: In the Vals AI benchmark, OpenAI's GPT-6 Sol Daybreak hits 80.8 percent of attack objectives in simulated corporate networks. Worse, the open-weight model DeepSeek V4.1 Flash reaches 72.8 percent at a tenth of the cost. Because open models can no longer be restricted, analysts say the window for defenders is shrinking fast....

items.title: Ripple-65B Preview delivers strong agentic coding results as a fully Apache 2.0 open US model
items.summary: Ricursive Intelligence is releasing Ripple-65B Preview, a 65-billion-parameter open-weight language model that the company says achieves the top score among open-source U.S. models on the TerminalBench 2.1 coding benchmark at a total R&D cost of $32 million. On other benchmarks, however, Ripple falls behind the likewise newly released western open model Inkling 2 Small....

items.title: Measuring how AI agents handle everyday wet-lab science
items.summary: OpenAI introduces BioBasicsBench, a 100-task benchmark measuring how well AI agents interpret raw experimental data and handle everyday wet-lab science.

items.title: Partnering with Hacktron to find vulnerabilities in OpenAI’s systems
items.summary: OpenAI is partnering with Hacktron to find vulnerabilities, test connections with third-party services, and strengthen defenses with frontier AI.

items.title: Setting a new standard for responsible AI infrastructure
items.summary: OpenAI introduces its National Community Compact and Compute Campus Policy Blueprint to protect local resources, create jobs, and guide responsible AI infrastructure development.

items.title: Perplexity now has its own always-on AI agent
items.summary: Perplexity is launching "Teammates," always-on agents that work through ongoing projects on their own virtual machines. The feature requires the Max plan at $200 per month, well above similar offerings from OpenAI or Anthropic. The market for always-on agents is getting crowded. The article Perplexity now has its own always-on AI agent appeared first on The Decoder .

items.title: Megaspeed exec was recruited to spy on Nvidia CEO, according to US intelligence memo
items.summary: A memo circulated earlier this year reportedly claimed that China’s Ministry of State Security recruited a female technology executive to spy on Nvidia's CEO.

items.title: OpenAI reportedly raises an additional $11 billion at a $1.25 trillion valuation
items.summary: OpenAI has reportedly raised an additional $11 billion as part of a funding round that hasn't closed yet but is expected to in the coming weeks.

items.title: Hundreds of Artex AI hacking tools found publicly exposed to the web
items.summary: Security researchers found hundreds of servers hosting the penetration testing tool Artex exposed to the internet, allowing anyone access to the hacking tool.
